title: TrueNorth.bet trademark, website and licensing timeline
summary: Trace the TrueNorth.bet name from a Canadian trademark filing in 2021 through archived homepages and Kahnawà:ke’s 2024 suspension and 2025 revocation decisions.
context: The trademark register dates the claim to the name. The gaming commission records the operator’s authorization. Its December 2024 suspension names www.truenorth.bet, while its August 2025 revocation names www.truenorthbets.com. The commission identifies True North in both decisions. A dated archive response can outlast a regulatory decision and cannot establish whether bets were accepted.
related: Read the True North operator record and the interval between decisions
events: The Canadian Intellectual Property Office (CIPO) records application 2,090,183 for the name TrueNorth.bet. The filing predates the first homepage capture in this timeline.
The Wayback CDX index lists a successful HTTPS capture of truenorth.bet. This is the earliest observation in the saved sample.
Page 957 of Canada’s Trademarks Journal lists TrueNorth.bet under class 41 for online casino games and video games.
A later successful capture records the website at its www hostname.
CIPO registered the mark as TMA1171288. The register showed the status as registered when checked on November 27, 2026.
Kahnawà:ke’s commission directed the site named in the notice, www.truenorth.bet, to cease offering interactive gaming effective that day.
The Wayback availability index reports a successful response for truenorth.bet three days before the revocation took effect.
The commission published this decision on August 21 and dated the revocation to August 20. The revocation page identifies www.truenorthbets.com.

title: CIRA.ca registration and early website history
summary: Compare the registry’s 1998 registration date for cira.ca with a preserved 2005 homepage and a 2026 registry change.
context: Registration records describe the domain in the registry. An archived homepage shows what the archive captured at a particular time. A registry change can update technical or administrative fields without changing the website.
related: Explore the Canadian domain history example
events: The .ca RDAP service dates registration to February 5, 1998.
